items.rationale: The washing-machine leak qualifies as escape of water under §2.4.2, and §7.1.7(h) covers necessary cleaning of the affected floor. Allow €80 gross as this line's share of the comparable Case 12 bundle.
The hallway floor was also damaged by the escape of water, so necessary cleaning is covered under §7.1.7(h). Allow €90 gross, bringing the combined floor-cleaning allowance to €170.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the source and confirming that it no longer leaks, even if the appliance itself is uninsured. Allow €85 gross for the check, with no appliance repair or separate call-out added.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged skirting
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(a) covers dismantling and disposal of affected finishes. Allow €65 gross for removal and disposal, separate from replacement.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like replacement of damaged skirting. Allow €150 gross for supply and fitting, bringing lines 1–5 to €470, within the Case 12 range.

items.description: Clean and repaint unaffected upstairs bedroom
items.rationale: Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude work in rooms not physically affected by the leak. No part of this line is payable.

items.description: Measure moisture in the two affected floors
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary moisture measurements in the damaged areas. Allow €185 gross for the two adjoining areas, calibrated to the €153–178 single-kitchen measurement in Case 21.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary floor drying, but §7.1.8(c) bars duplicate costs. Allow €205 gross for distinct drying work, excluding the separately billed equipment rental and worker hours.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers necessary drying equipment hire, provided it is not already included in the drying charge under §7.1.8(c). Allow €100 gross, bringing lines 7–10 to €642, within the Case 12 range.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour at customary rates, subject to the duplicate-cost exclusion in §7.1.8(c). The supplied gross prior gives 4 × €38 = €152.

items.description: Measure moisture and dry basement storage room
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) exclude drying and associated measurements in a separate room with no documented damage. No part of this line is payable.

Section 5.2.6 covers specialist transport only from the balance remaining after restoration takes priority under the €1,190 gross per-item cap. Restoration is likely to exhaust the cap; if sufficient balance remains, allow €90 gross for transport, the first ancillary measure invoiced.
Section 5.2.6 includes the specialist assessment, but the cap is applied first to restoration and then to transport before this line. If a balance reaches this line, estimate a €110 gross allowance.
Section 5.2.6 covers drying and stabilisation only from the balance left after restoration, transport and assessment. If a balance reaches this line, estimate a €120 gross allowance.

Although §4.3(d) excludes household contents as insured property, §5.2.6 covers specialist restoration of this damaged valuable painting and gives restoration first call on the cap. Full restoration is likely to reach the unscheduled-item limit of €1,000 net × 1.19 = €1,190 gross, assuming VAT was incurred under §7.7.
Section 5.2.6 applies only to an item affected by the insured event. The second painting was unaffected, so no restoration cost is payable.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separately charged administrative and processing overhead, and §5.2.6 does not list it as a conservation measure. No amount is payable.
